facts.statement: The study used a mouse model of brain bleeding created by injecting an enzyme into the brain.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Human brain vessel cells were grown in a lab dish and exposed to a substance that mimics the environment after a brain bleed, along with the protein Gal-3.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: In the brain cells, the protein Gal-3 attached to a receptor called TLR4 and stopped its normal breakdown, causing the receptor to build up.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The buildup of the receptor triggered a chain of chemical signals that increased the production of an enzyme which breaks down the proteins that seal the blood-brain barrier.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The researchers concluded that this process leads to the breakdown of the barrier that protects the brain from the bloodstream.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue
